findings.obligation: P6: 'no link is left focusable or announced while it is invisible'; the design observes 'the set of rail links that can take the keyboard focus while they are invisible' and names clipped as one way a member is invisible (architecture.md:670). Both feature files advertise clipping as the RED-trigger.
findings.observation: OPEN, fix REFUTED at ef1a4be, severity unchanged (non-blocking). The hit test was added as asked, but hitsItsOwnCentre returns true for `hit === el || el.contains(hit) || hit.contains(el)`. A member clipped away by clip, clip-path or an ancestor's overflow keeps its layout box and paints nothing at its centre, so elementFromPoint returns an ancestor - and every ancestor up to document.documentElement contains the member - which makes the third clause true in exactly the case the test was added to catch. The new clause can therefore only fail for a member covered by an element that is neither its ancestor nor its descendant. The same file implements the correct form for the label 250 lines down (hit === label || label.contains(hit)), which is also the form the design states. The module doc now contradicts itself: 'without it, a destination clipped away while it keeps its box would read as visible' is still true with it. Separately, FOCUS_PROBE's own `visible` field - the one the toggle lane reads for 'nothing invisible takes the focus' - was given no hit test at all. Not blocking: the mechanisms this slice could plausibly regress into (width, zero size, opacity, display, visibility) are observed, and the design forbids clipping a member away.
findings.remediation: Drop the `|| hit.contains(el)` clause: a member that paints at its own centre always hit-tests to itself or to a descendant, so the two remaining clauses admit every legitimate case. Apply the same test to FOCUS_PROBE's `visible` so the toggle lane's consumer is not left layout-only, and correct the module-doc paragraph that claims the clipped case is caught. Oracle-owned, out of band: the crafter must not edit oracle files, so this is for the acceptance designer before this lane is cited as completion evidence for P6's invisible-focusable law.

The not-observed column absorbed the pixel magnitude and the choice between comparing against the same label unfocused or its unfocused siblings, so the oracle keeps its freedom where no promise lives.

FINDING 1 VERIFIED FIXED (icon drawn). assert_rail_offers now takes a RailShape and every call site passes the geometry it read: Narrow for the reachability row, the phone row and the narrow comeback row; Open for the desk-width Given, both no-script rows and the open comeback row. The Open arm's no-glyph-beside-the-words assertion moved INTO the same function, so it is now taken wherever the open geometry is read rather than only on the way into the narrow one - strictly more coverage than the round-1 bytes. The 8px floor is declared in the code as a floor rather than a design value, bounds no product value (Lucide glyphs ship far larger) and fixes no pixel promise, so it does not couple the oracle to a design choice. FINDING 2 VERIFIED FIXED (focused label is now a differential), and it matches the authority the design published in e46b567. The When takes a read_nav of the rail with the focus cleared BEFORE walking, and stores {unfocused, walk} as one record, so the pair is one differential of one page rather than two unrelated measurements. The Then matches each rail stop to its unfocused member by the member's own word and requires labelPresent && labelInTheLayout && focused height >= 1 && focused width >= clipped width + MATERIALLY_WIDER_PX (8.0). labelShown is gone from FOCUS_PROBE and is replaced by labelBox, labelInTheLayout and labelCentreHitsTheLabel, the last computed as hit === label || label.contains(hit) - the correct form, no ancestor clause - and carried only in the failure message, never as the verdict. FINDING 3 FIX REFUTED, and it stays open at the same non-blocking severity. The hit test was added as asked, but hitsItsOwnCentre accepts `hit.contains(el)` as well as `hit === el || el.contains(hit)`. A member clipped away by clip, clip-path or an ancestor's overflow keeps its layout box and paints nothing at its centre, so document.elementFromPoint returns whatever paints there - an ancestor - and every ancestor, up to document.documentElement, contains the member. So the third clause is TRUE in precisely the case the hit test was added to catch, and visibleNow still reads a clipped-away destination as visible. The only state the new clause can fail is a member covered by an element that is neither its ancestor nor its descendant. Separately, FOCUS_PROBE's own `visible` field - the one the nav-collapse-toggle lane reads at feature_nav_collapse.rs:947 for 'nothing invisible takes the focus' - was not given any hit test at all, so that consumer stays layout-only.
